info.title: CycleCalcs Astronomy API
info.description: A read-only astronomy API that returns the named answer and the numbers behind it, with the frame, epoch, time scale and refraction model stated on every response. It reports angles, times and names, and attaches no meaning to any of them. Computed in real time with the MIT-licensed Astronomy Engine. This document is generated from the shipped route table (netlify/lib/v2/registry.mjs) by tools/generate-openapi.mjs, so it cannot list a route, a parameter or a requirement the API does not actually enforce. Computed astronomical output is unrestricted: use, store, redistribute and sell it without attribution. The one exception is GeoNames place data served by GET /v2/places and by any response that resolved a `place` parameter, which requires the credit line in meta.attribution; see GET /v2/attribution for the full source register.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: The instant to evaluate, or a comma-separated list of up to 24 instants (at=t1,t2,...), each read by the rules below. A list returns data.series with one row per entry, in the order sent, and echoes query.mode list; it is capped on its length, not on the time between its entries, and is not paged. ISO 8601: a date (2026-06-21), or a date and time with an optional seconds, fraction and either Z or a numeric UTC offset (+hh:mm, no seconds). The basic format without separators (20260621, 20260621T210000Z, +hhmm) reads the same. No offset and no `tz` reads as UTC. Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, read as UTC whatever `tz` says: jd:2461000.5 is 2025-11-21T00:00:00Z. Reliable from 1700 to 2200.

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: Sampling stride for a range query: a number plus a unit, one of min, m (minute), h (hour), d (day), w (week), mo (month) or y (year), for example 1h, 6h or 1d. Resolves to at least 1 minute and at most 1 year. Needs `start`. This is the generic grammar; an endpoint that narrows it documents the narrowing on its own `step` parameter, and /v2/conventions publishes every narrowing under limits.step_grammar.endpoint_policies.

parameters.name: bodies
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of targets, up to 20: any of sun, moon, mercury, venus, earth, mars, jupiter, saturn, uranus, neptune, pluto, star:<name> or hr:<n> for a named star (one of 80: the 57 navigational stars of the Nautical Almanac, Polaris, and the IAU-named stars of V 3.0 or brighter within 10.3 deg of the ecliptic, listed at /v2/enums?set=stars; names match on letters and digits, so star:kaus_australis works; proper motion is applied to the date), or radec:<ra>,<dec>[,j2000] entries. Mutually exclusive with `body`.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: A single target: one of sun, moon, mercury, venus, earth, mars, jupiter, saturn, uranus, neptune, pluto, star:<name> or hr:<n> for a named star (one of 80: the 57 navigational stars of the Nautical Almanac, Polaris, and the IAU-named stars of V 3.0 or brighter within 10.3 deg of the ecliptic, listed at /v2/enums?set=stars; names match on letters and digits, so star:kaus_australis works; proper motion is applied to the date), or radec:<ra>,<dec>[,j2000] for a fixed celestial point (right ascension in decimal hours, declination in decimal degrees). Mutually exclusive with `bodies`.

parameters.name: frames
parameters.description: Which coordinate frame families to include: minimal is of-date equatorial and horizontal only; standard adds equatorial J2000, true ecliptic-of-date, horizontal and distance; all adds ecliptic J2000 and galactic.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.description: Measured from the center of the Earth, or the center of the Sun. Earth itself has no geocentric position and needs frame=heliocentric.

parameters.name: refraction
parameters.description: normal applies Saemundsson refraction to apparent altitude; none reports the unrefracted geometric altitude.

TropicalSign.description: The 30-degree sector of the body's apparent ecliptic longitude in the true ecliptic and equinox of date (frame ect), counted from the moving March equinox: Aries 0 to 30 deg, Taurus 30 to 60 deg, and so on to Pisces 330 to 360 deg. A named coordinate bin, not a constellation: because the equinox precesses, the bins drift against the stars by about 1 deg every 71.6 years, at the measured IAU 2006 precession rate. Taken from the geocentric place on /v2/positions, /v2/moon and /v2/planet-board, even when lat and lon make a position block topocentric: /v2/positions says so in meta.conventions.label_origin and /v2/planet-board in position.ecliptic_origin. With a location the Moon's topocentric longitude can sit up to about 1 deg from the geocentric one its sector is taken from. On /v2/sun, which always has a location, it is taken from the topocentric place, at most about 9 arcsec from the geocentric one. Emitted for Solar System bodies only.

code.description: The sector name as a stable lower-case code.

sign_index.description: The sector number, 0 for 0 to 30 deg through 11 for 330 to 360 deg.

degree_in_sign.description: Degrees of longitude past the start of the sector, from 0 up to but not including 30. The bound is written as a plain maximum so the OpenAPI 3.0 copy stays valid.

Constellation.description: The IAU constellation containing the position: one of the 88 regions whose boundaries Delporte drew for the IAU in 1930 along lines of right ascension and declination of the B1875.0 equinox. The J2000 right ascension and declination are precessed to B1875.0 and looked up there. A body off the ecliptic can sit outside the zodiac constellations, so the constellation and tropical_sign often disagree: Saturn at 2026-10-04T12:00:00Z is at ecliptic longitude 11.30 deg and latitude -2.71 deg, in the Aries bin of tropical_sign and in the constellation Cetus. Taken from the geocentric place on /v2/positions, /v2/moon, /v2/today, /v2/retrogrades and /v2/planet-events, even when lat and lon make a position block topocentric, and on /v2/positions from the heliocentric place under frame=heliocentric. On /v2/planet-board (with a location, unless frames=minimal) and /v2/sun it is taken from the topocentric place, which sits at most the body's parallax from the geocentric one: about 9 arcsec for the Sun and 33 arcsec for Venus at its closest. On /v2/positions it is also given for named star and radec targets.

LabelOrigin.description: On /v2/positions, meta.conventions.label_origin: the place every row's tropical_sign and constellation were taken from, one value for the whole response, present when some row carries either label. It is geocentric, except that under frame=heliocentric the constellation is taken from the heliocentric place and label_origin says heliocentric, and no tropical_sign is emitted. Never topocentric, even when a row's position block is. A named star or radec row has a constellation and no tropical_sign.
